rationales.F02: Previous control with verapamil suggests a possible atrial tachycardia component.
rationales.F04: Lack of response to amiodarone may indicate a non-reentrant tachycardia mechanism.
rationales.F07: Cannon A waves suggest atrioventricular dissociation, which is more typical of atrial tachycardia with block.
rationales.F08: Regular tachycardia at 130 beats per minute is a hallmark of atrial tachycardia and supraventricular tachycardia.
rationales.F09: Incomplete right bundle branch block morphology can be seen in atrial tachycardia with aberrancy.
rationales.F11: Left-axis deviation can be seen in atrial tachycardias originating from the left atrium.
rationales.F12: Sustained tachycardia throughout the monitoring period supports a diagnosis of atrial tachycardia.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of incomplete right bundle branch block morphology and left-axis deviation specifically supports Atrial Tachycardia with Block.
